newsitem.title: HUNGARY: HUNGARY TO DECIDE TV TENDER WINNERS END JUNE.
newsitem.headline: HUNGARY TO DECIDE TV TENDER WINNERS END JUNE.

text.p: The winners of the tenders for Hungary's two soon-to-be-launched commercial TV channels will be announced by the end of June, two weeks later than planned, the national TV and radio body ORTT said on Tuesday.

Hungary's media privatisation has been beset with delays since the media law, passed in December 1995 after four years of bitter political dispute, opened the way for the privatisation of the country's state-controlled national television and radio market.
ORTT president Mihaly T. Revesz told a media conference in this central Hungarian holiday resort that this latest delay of two weeks was to be expected.
"The process of media transformation took 10 to 15 years in Western Europe...we had 14 months,"
Three bidders are in the race for ten-year concessions for two national commercial TV channels, on offer for eight billion forints plus 25 per cent VAT each, three years payable in advance.
The Swedish-Hungairan consortium of SBS-MTM submitted a bid for one channel, a consortium of CLT and UFA for the other while U.S.-based Central European Media Enterprises is in the race for both.
Only consortia were allowed to bid, no single company is allowed to have more than a 49 percent stake, while Hungarians have to hold a minimum of 26 percent.
Under Hungary's media law, the winners have to go on air three months after the concession contracts have been signed.

Revesz acknowledged that ORTT, set up in March 1996, shortly after Hungary's media law was passed, had been accused of being "expensive, inexperienced and not doing its job" but said he rejected the allegations.
He said this year ORTT will generate income of 22 billion forints compared with operational costs of some 500 million forints.
Analysts estimated that the two national commercial channels could capture 30 percent of the market each.
Revesz said he expects the privatisation of Hungary's media to create thousands of new jobs over the next few years.
"My vision is that the...industry will employ 70,000 to 80,000 people in the future," he said.
ORTT said on Friday it had drafted the tender for seven-year concessions for two nationwide radio channels and and rejected criticism that the asking price was too high.

The price for each seven-year radio channel concession has been set at three billion forints plus 25 percent VAT, with 30 percent payable in advance and the rest in four annual instalments beginning with the third year of the concession.
Several potential bidders have said that such terms could jeopardise profitability.
